t: The Mexica built Tenochtitlan on a small swampy island in Lake Texcoco, enlarging it with chinampas, and it became the largest city in the pre-Columbian Americas.
As capital of the Aztec Empire in the 15th century it had causeways, canals, aqueducts, a walled ceremonial centre of about 45 buildings and a population estimated at 200,000 to 400,000.
Cortés besieged it for over 90 days, disease struck its people, and it fell on 13 August 1521 to the Spanish and Tlaxcaltec; Mexico City was founded on the ruins.
dyk: In 1987 archaeologists found 1,789 human bones five metres below a Mexico City street, a burial of the 1480s at the foot of the main temple of Tenochtitlan.
ev: The Mexica found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco, by the date now given
The levee of Nezahualcoyotl is completed under Moctezuma I
Tenochtitlan fights a war against its neighbour Tlatelolco
Ahuitzotl begins to rule, and the city is rebuilt after a flood
Hernán Cortés arrives in the city on 8 November
The city falls on 13 August to the Spanish and Tlaxcaltec
Major excavations of the Templo Mayor begin

f.founded: By the Mexica on a small island in Lake Texcoco; the exact date is unclear, and 13 March 1325 was chosen in 1925 for the 600th anniversary
f.where: On an island in what was Lake Texcoco, in the Valley of Mexico, now the historic centre of Mexico City, Mexico
f.known: Capital of the Aztec Empire; the Templo Mayor; the chinampas; causeways and canals; the market of Tlatelolco; the palace of Moctezuma; the fall of 1521
f.today: Its ruins lie in the historic centre of Mexico City, which Cortés founded on the site.
